q: Compare the trends in the two kinds of pond.
With weak predators the mean rose from 11 to 14 spots; with strong predators it fell from 11 to 7.
Calculate the percentage change in mean spots with weak predators.
Explain the trend with strong predators by natural selection.
Males vary in spot number. Brightly spotted males are seen and eaten more often, so duller males survive and reproduce more; spot number is inherited, so the mean falls.
Explain why spots increase where predators are weak.
Females prefer colourful males (sexual selection); with little predation, more spots means more mates and more offspring.
Suggest why the change happened within only 20 generations.
Strong selection, a short generation time (a few months) and plenty of existing variation.
